title: Gilgal
lead: Israel's first camp in Canaan, near Jericho, where Joshua set up twelve stones from the Jordan. It became a shrine where Samuel judged and Saul was made king, and later a target of the prophets (Joshua 4–5; 1 Samuel 11; Amos 4:4).

sections.b: At Gilgal Israel set up the stones from the Jordan, circumcised the new generation and kept its first Passover in the land (Joshua 4:19–5:12). It remained Joshua's base (Joshua 9:6; Joshua 10:6). Samuel judged there on his yearly circuit and renewed the kingdom there for Saul (1 Samuel 7:16; 1 Samuel 11:14–15); there Saul offered sacrifice without waiting and was rejected (1 Samuel 13:8–14; 1 Samuel 15:12–33). By the 8th century it had become a center of worship that Hosea and Amos condemned (Hosea 4:15; Amos 4:4; Amos 5:5). Micah remembers the journey "from Shittim to Gilgal" as a lesson in God's saving acts (Micah 6:5). There may have been more than one place called Gilgal (Deuteronomy 11:30; 2 Kings 2:1).
